# Stable IDs for cross-references, generated by DanKG

## Context

`[[Heading]]` resolves by slug, searched across the whole corpus at
graph-build time (`graph/resolve.md`'s `resolve_wiki`, `find_slug`).
This is cheap and needs no separate index, but it ties a link's
validity to the heading's own text: rename "Alphabet" to "The
Alphabet" and every `[[Alphabet]]` pointing at it either goes
dangling or, worse, silently re-resolves to some other heading that
now shares the slug. Tools built around a persistent backlink
database (org-roam is the comparison point that prompted this plan)
sidestep the problem with a stable identifier -- a UUID stored in the
node itself, independent of title or filename -- so a rename never
touches what a link actually points at.

That identifier does not require a database. It only requires two
things DanKG already has: a place in the file to keep it, and a
corpus-wide walk to resolve it against, the same walk `find_slug`
already does. What DanKG does not have is any way to *mint* one. This
plan is that: `dankg` generates and writes the ID itself, so a reader
never hand-types or maintains a random token.

Nothing here has shipped. See *Phased build order*, below, for what a
first implementation would actually touch.

## Mechanism

### ID shape

Not a real UUID. DanKG's own `<!-- dankg:result name=x hash=... -->`
marker already carries a 16-hex-digit token (`hash::hex`, a
fixed-width `u64`, `src/hash.md`), and an ID in the same shape reads
as one more DanKG marker, not a second, unrelated notation borrowed
from elsewhere. The value itself has to come from somewhere other
than `hash::fnv1a`, though: `fnv1a` is a *content* hash, deterministic
on its input, and two headings created with identical starting text
would collide if their ID were derived from content the same way a
result hash is. An ID needs actual randomness, not a hash of
anything.

Zero-dependency randomness is a solved problem elsewhere in this
codebase (decision 1): `term.md`'s raw-mode/`ioctl` code reaches
`extern "C"` instead of a crate for OS access `std` does not expose.
The same pattern reads a handful of bytes from `/dev/urandom` for an
ID's own entropy, on the platforms DanKG already targets. Collision
risk at a personal corpus's scale is not worth spending more machinery
on than that -- this is an identifier for "which heading," not a
security token.

### Storage: a marker comment, not a heading attribute

CommonMark headings have no attribute syntax (`# Heading {#id}` is a
Pandoc/kramdown extension, not CommonMark). CommonMark *does* define
HTML comments as an inert block/inline construct, which is exactly
what `dankg:result` and `dankg:depends` (`src/depends.md`) already
build on. An ID marker follows the identical shape:

```markdown
# Some Heading
<!-- dankg:id 3f9a7c21e08b445d -->
```

A stock CommonMark renderer sees an invisible comment and nothing
else changes. `depends.md`'s `parse_marker` is the precedent for the
line-reading itself -- a small, dedicated scanner
(`line.trim().strip_prefix("<!--")?...`), not a detour through the
general block parser. Attaching a marker to *which heading it
belongs to*, though, is `eval::result::locate_existing`'s job to
mirror, not `depends`'s: a `dankg:depends` marker names its own
target explicitly (`target=#other`) and can sit anywhere in the
document, while `dankg:result` is found positionally, by checking
whether the block immediately after a specific code block is a lone
marker line. `dankg:id` needs that same positional check, just
anchored to a heading instead of a code block: the block right after
a heading, if it is a lone `dankg:id` line, belongs to it.

### Resolution: the same walk, one more field

`Node` (`graph/model.md`) gains a new field, e.g.
`stable_id: Option<String>`, populated during `graph::build`'s own
node construction (`graph/build.md`) -- a new read point there, not
a reuse of `depends::markers_in`, which only ever runs from
`dankg check` and never touches `Node` construction at all.
`depends.md` is still the right precedent for the *scanner itself* (a
small, dedicated line-reader, not a detour through the general block
parser); it just plugs into a different call site than
`dankg:depends` does. Resolving a link by ID is `find_slug`'s
sibling, not its replacement: a linear scan (or a small `HashMap`,
built and dropped in the same call) over `stable_id` instead of
`id.slug`, on the exact same corpus-wide node list `resolve_wiki`
already has in hand. No new index survives past the walk that builds
it, matching every other lookup this module already does. There is
nothing here a database would do that a second field on `Node`, plus
one more match arm in `resolve_wiki`, do not already cover.

### Reference syntax

`[[id:3f9a7c21e08b445d]]` -- a new prefix recognized inside the
existing `[[...]]` form, checked first in `resolve_wiki` before the
current-file/other-file/slug cases it already has. No new bracket
syntax, no new link form a reader has to learn separately from the
wikilinks they already write.

### Generation

Two entry points, matching how the rest of DanKG already offers both
a batch command and an interactive one for related jobs (`dankg fmt`/
`dankg check` for the corpus-wide pass, `[tui] commands` for
on-demand):

- `dankg id <path>...` -- walks the named files, writes a fresh
  `dankg:id` marker under every heading that does not already carry
  one, skips every heading that does. Idempotent by construction: a
  second run touches nothing a first run already handled.
- A TUI key, bound the same way `keys.eval` already is, that assigns
  one to the selected heading on demand and reloads -- for "I want to
  link to this specific heading right now," without leaving the
  session to run a separate command.

Both write through the same marker format and the same "skip if
already present" rule, so it does not matter which one a reader
reaches for first.

## Design decisions

### Why not a database

A database earns its cost on three things this plan does not need:
arbitrary queries over the corpus (SQL joins DanKG's own graph model
does not expose today, ID-based linking or not), incremental lookup
at a scale where a full corpus walk stops being cheap, and identifier
uniqueness *enforcement* across concurrent writers. DanKG's actual
failure mode -- a rename breaking a slug-based link -- is fixed by the
identifier existing at all, in the plaintext, resolved by the walk
already in place. A separate index would be one more thing that can
drift out of sync with the files it is supposed to describe, which is
exactly the state decision 1's zero-dependency, no-hidden-store
posture already refuses to accept elsewhere in this codebase.

### Staleness: the one hash this must never become

**Every hash DanKG computes today is a source hash, checked for
drift, never trusted past the moment the source it covers changes**
(architecture.md, the `SELECT`-result rationale). `dankg:id` must be
the deliberate exception. It is not a hash of the heading's content --
it has no "fresh" value to compare against, because nothing about it
is ever supposed to change once written. `dankg check` must never
gain a code path that treats a `dankg:id` marker as something that
can go stale, the way a `dankg:result` marker's own `hash=` can. The
one failure mode worth guarding against explicitly: a future change
that generalizes `check`'s "does this marker's hash match a fresh
one" logic and accidentally sweeps `dankg:id` up in it, since the two
markers otherwise look alike on the page.

### Collision handling

Astronomically unlikely at a 64-bit random value and a personal
corpus's node count, but not impossible, and cheap to check for free
during the same walk that resolves links: `dankg id`, writing a new
marker, checks the fresh value against every `stable_id` already
collected and re-rolls on the rare hit rather than trusting single-try
uniqueness. The one real collision case -- two branches independently
running `dankg id` on the same new heading before merging -- is
inherent to any offline-minted identifier, org-roam's own UUIDs
included, and not something this plan can or needs to close.

## What this doesn't solve

Slug-based linking stays exactly as it is; `dankg:id` is additive,
not a migration every existing `[[Heading]]` link has to make. A
corpus with no `dankg:id` markers anywhere behaves identically to
today. This also does not give DanKG anything like org-roam's live
backlink buffer or full-text search -- those are database features,
and this plan is deliberately not proposing one, per the section
above.

## Phased build order

**Status**: not started. Nothing in this section has a line of code
behind it yet.

**Phase 1** -- marker format and parsing: `dankg:id` recognized by a
`depends.md`-style line-scanner, wired into `graph::build`'s own node
construction (`graph/build.md`) rather than reusing
`depends::markers_in` -- that function only ever runs from
`dankg check`, never touches `Node`, and stays exactly as it is.
`Node.stable_id` added (`graph/model.md`), populated at the point
`graph::build` already reads the rest of a heading's own data.

**Phase 2** -- resolution: `resolve_wiki` (`graph/resolve.md`) gains
the `id:` prefix case, checked first, falling through to the existing
cases unchanged for everything else. Dangling-link diagnostics for an
unresolved `[[id:...]]` follow the same shape `find_slug`'s own
failure path already reports.

**Phase 3** -- generation: the zero-dependency random-bytes source
(`/dev/urandom` via `extern "C"`, mirroring `term.md`'s own OS-access
pattern), `dankg id <path>...` as a new CLI command
(`main.md`/`cmd.md`), and its own write-back function. `eval/result.md`'s
`write_back` is not directly callable here -- it always inserts a
result marker *and* a fenced output block together, a shape
`dankg:id` does not need -- but it is the precedent for the technique:
split the source on `\n`, splice one new line in at the computed
position, rejoin, preserving whether the file had a trailing newline.
The new function is smaller than `write_back`, not a variant of it.

**Phase 4** -- TUI key: a new binding in `event_loop`
(`tui/app.md`), assigning an ID to `app.selected` on demand and
calling `reload()` afterward, the same shape every other mutating key
already follows.

**Phase 5** -- harden and document: collision re-roll on write,
`dankg check` explicitly confirmed to leave `dankg:id` markers alone
(a test pinning this, not just a read of the code, given the
staleness risk called out above), `architecture.md` gets a real
decision entry once this actually ships, `README.md` documents the
`[[id:...]]` form alongside the existing link table.

## Critical files

- `src/depends.md` -- the precedent for the marker line-scanner
  itself; `dankg:id`'s own parser is this shape, not a new one.
- `src/eval/result.md` -- two separate precedents, not one:
  `locate_existing`'s positional check (the block right after a given
  block, matched by name) for finding a heading's own `dankg:id`
  marker, and `write_back`'s splice-and-rejoin technique for a new,
  smaller write-back function -- neither is directly callable for
  `dankg:id`, both are the shape to follow.
- `src/hash.md` -- `hash::hex`'s fixed-width formatting, reused for
  the ID's own string form even though its value comes from a
  different source than `fnv1a`.
- `src/graph/model.md` -- `Node`, where `stable_id` is added.
- `src/graph/resolve.md` -- `resolve_wiki`, where the `id:` prefix is
  checked.
- `src/tui/term.md` -- the `extern "C"`-not-a-crate precedent random
  byte generation follows.
- `architecture.md` -- the `SELECT`-result staleness rationale this
  plan's own *Staleness* section leans on, and where a real decision
  entry belongs once this ships.

## Verification

- Unit tests for the marker parser: recognized, malformed, and absent
  cases, matching `depends.md`'s own test shape.
- A round-trip test: `dankg id` on a fresh heading, then a
  `[[id:...]]` link elsewhere in the same corpus resolving to it.
- A rename test: change a heading's title, confirm a `[[id:...]]`
  link to it still resolves while a hypothetical slug-based link to
  the old title would not -- the entire point of this plan, pinned as
  an actual assertion rather than left implicit.
- A `dankg check` test confirming a `dankg:id` marker is never
  reported stale, however its heading's own content changes.
- `dankg fmt --check` / `dankg check .` after re-tangling every
  touched `.md` file via the standard edit loop (`CLAUDE.md`).
- `cargo tree` / `Cargo.lock` unchanged through every phase -- this
  plan should cost DanKG zero new dependencies, the same property
  `plans/eval-custom-plan.md` holds itself to.
